Method

The following are proposed buyer procedures derived from the reviewed evidence, not reports of completed supplier trials. They do not recommend a universal winner. Each use case states the required deliverable, a candidate responsibility model, a paid pilot and acceptance evidence. The buyer should pre-register critical errors, slices, exclusions, rework limits and decision rules before seeing outputs. Numeric targets should follow the buyer’s risk and uncertainty requirements; no universal accuracy threshold is invented here.

Expert preference data for a specialized assistant

Analysis

Buyer use case 1 — Expert preference data for a specialized assistant: requirement and comparison. Specify prompts, candidate responses, domain credentials, language, independent judgments per item, preference strength and rationale fields. Compare a managed preference program with participant access only after assigning task design, recruitment, adjudication and acceptance. HelpSteer3, HelpSteer2 and InstructGPT show why final pair counts conceal different repetition and aggregation structures.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus, repair20261111.claim.current-reference145, next.claim.helpsteer2.qa, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets

Analysis

Buyer use case 1 — Expert preference data for a specialized assistant: proposed paid pilot. Use a paid calibration batch spanning routine, ambiguous and deliberately difficult cases. Freeze the raw-label schema before consensus. Have a separate reviewer inspect disagreements and rejected items without knowing the supplier or initial majority. Keep duplicate prompts and ranked-set expansion identifiable, then hold out a second batch for acceptance.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus, repair20261111.claim.current-reference145, next.claim.helpsteer2.qa, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets

Analysis

Buyer use case 1 — Expert preference data for a specialized assistant: proposed acceptance and limits. Accept only against the predeclared target: valid independent judgments, traceable exclusions, correct domain-language intersections and adjudication supported by reasons. Report first-pass and final acceptance with all submitted items in the denominator. Do not let post-filter agreement substitute for coverage of difficult cases. Reject an unsupported claim that more released pairs necessarily means more independent human evidence.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus, repair20261111.claim.current-reference145, next.claim.helpsteer2.qa, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets

Repository engineering and coding-agent environments

Analysis

Buyer use case 2 — Repository engineering and coding-agent environments: requirement and comparison. Define repository language/version, issue requirements, permitted tools, test suite, reset behavior, task horizon and artifact rights. Compare custom environment builders, engineering teams and licensed task packages on the same accepted unit. G2i’s contract boundary and A.Team’s engagement models require special attention when responsibility for the final environment could remain with the buyer.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring, next.claim.swebench.evaluation, cohort4.claim.mbpp.test-overfit, repair20261111.claim.current-reference192, candidate.cohort5.a-team.delivery-model, candidate.cohort5.hackerrank.rl-package

Analysis

Buyer use case 2 — Repository engineering and coding-agent environments: proposed paid pilot. Run known-correct, known-incorrect and superficially passing patches in isolated copies. Repeat resets and tests, record installation/network failures separately and sample passing changes for completeness, readability and unintended behavior. Freeze the environment image, dependencies, time limits and verifier version. Inspect a hidden test that catches a plausible shortcut rather than merely reproducing the reference implementation.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring, next.claim.swebench.evaluation, cohort4.claim.mbpp.test-overfit, repair20261111.claim.current-reference192, candidate.cohort5.a-team.delivery-model, candidate.cohort5.hackerrank.rl-package

Analysis

Buyer use case 2 — Repository engineering and coding-agent environments: proposed acceptance and limits. Accept reproducible environments and task-scoped outcomes under the agreed protocol, with infrastructure failures explicitly adjudicated. Require pass/fail consistency, regression protection and side-effect review. SWE-bench cautions that passing tests does not guarantee complete solutions, while MBPP shows hard-coded-input gaming. A supplier’s benchmark authorship or engineering credentials alone does not satisfy these tests.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring, next.claim.swebench.evaluation, cohort4.claim.mbpp.test-overfit, repair20261111.claim.current-reference192, candidate.cohort5.a-team.delivery-model, candidate.cohort5.hackerrank.rl-package

Enterprise browser and desktop workflow training

Analysis

Buyer use case 3 — Enterprise browser and desktop workflow training: requirement and comparison. Specify an initial state, user goal, authorized actions, protected data and prohibited side effects. Decide whether the deliverable is human demonstrations, a simulated environment, a verifier or all three. AfterQuery’s demonstrations, Abundant’s customer-workflow conversion and Refresh’s versioned visual checks represent different disclosed units. A recording without an outcome specification is not yet an accepted RL task.

Evidence: candidate.cohort4.afterquery.computer-use-demonstrations, candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.foundry-customer-offer, candidate.cohort4.refresh.versioned-verifiers, cohort4.claim.osworld.side-effect-gap, cohort4.dataset.claim.osworld.infrastructure, cohort4.claim.webshop.reward-verification-limit, cohort2.claim.webarena.hybrid-evaluation

Analysis

Buyer use case 3 — Enterprise browser and desktop workflow training: proposed paid pilot. Use synthetic or approved nonproduction accounts and fixed starting documents. Capture action traces, final state and constraint violations. Include recoverable mistakes, irreversible actions, ambiguous requests and tasks that should be refused. Test evaluator behavior on completed tasks with a deliberately harmful extra action, and on valid alternate solutions that differ from the reference sequence.

Evidence: candidate.cohort4.afterquery.computer-use-demonstrations, candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.foundry-customer-offer, candidate.cohort4.refresh.versioned-verifiers, cohort4.claim.osworld.side-effect-gap, cohort4.dataset.claim.osworld.infrastructure, cohort4.claim.webshop.reward-verification-limit, cohort2.claim.webarena.hybrid-evaluation

Analysis

Buyer use case 3 — Enterprise browser and desktop workflow training: proposed acceptance and limits. Require reproducible resets, authorized-state transitions and preservation of protected content, alongside end-goal success. OSWorld explicitly identifies side-effect detection limits and configuration failures; WebShop documents lexical reward errors; WebArena uses mixed semantic and state checks. Acceptance should distinguish environment, policy, model and judge failures so a low score does not silently become a provider-quality claim.

Evidence: candidate.cohort4.afterquery.computer-use-demonstrations, candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.foundry-customer-offer, candidate.cohort4.refresh.versioned-verifiers, cohort4.claim.osworld.side-effect-gap, cohort4.dataset.claim.osworld.infrastructure, cohort4.claim.webshop.reward-verification-limit, cohort2.claim.webarena.hybrid-evaluation

Multilingual assistant and localization evaluation

Analysis

Buyer use case 4 — Multilingual assistant and localization evaluation: requirement and comparison. State language variety, script, locale, domain, task type and whether native authoring or translation is required. Compare native task creation, post-edited translation and multilingual judging as different workflows. HelpSteer3’s missing intersections and M-IFEval’s language-specific constraint changes make a broad language count an inadequate specification.

Evidence: repair20261111.claim.current-reference145, cohort7.claim.mifeval.japanese-filter, cohort7.claim.mifeval.objective, cohort7.claim.menlo.dimensions, cohort7.claim.benchmax.postediting, cohort7.claim.multijudge.parallel-answers, cohort7.claim.multijudge.prompt

Analysis

Buyer use case 4 — Multilingual assistant and localization evaluation: proposed paid pilot. Construct a matrix of required language-domain pairs and sample every promised intersection. Use native-domain reviewers, preserve original and translated prompts and test local factuality, tone and instructions separately. Include constraints whose English formulation is invalid in the target script. Blind model identity and candidate order, then compare judge decisions with held-out human decisions under the actual target-language protocol.

Evidence: repair20261111.claim.current-reference145, cohort7.claim.mifeval.japanese-filter, cohort7.claim.mifeval.objective, cohort7.claim.menlo.dimensions, cohort7.claim.benchmax.postediting, cohort7.claim.multijudge.parallel-answers, cohort7.claim.multijudge.prompt

Analysis

Buyer use case 4 — Multilingual assistant and localization evaluation: proposed acceptance and limits. Accept documented coverage and calibrated errors within each required slice, with no unsupported extrapolation from an overall average. Report translation revisions and unresolved dialect disagreements. MENLO’s dimensions, BenchMAX’s post-editing and the multilingual-judge setup show why aggregate cross-language consistency cannot replace validity on the buyer’s real conversations.

Evidence: repair20261111.claim.current-reference145, cohort7.claim.mifeval.japanese-filter, cohort7.claim.mifeval.objective, cohort7.claim.menlo.dimensions, cohort7.claim.benchmax.postediting, cohort7.claim.multijudge.parallel-answers, cohort7.claim.multijudge.prompt

Medical, legal or financial expert data

Analysis

Buyer use case 5 — Medical, legal or financial expert data: requirement and comparison. Specify the permitted professional task, jurisdiction or clinical context, credential evidence, privacy boundary and intended model use. Shaip’s credential matching and Encord’s clinician/task matching are offering disclosures, while Aya Data’s Cydar case concerns specific image labels. Do not transfer evidence from image annotation to clinical advice quality or from general finance work to jurisdiction-specific legal accuracy.

Evidence: candidate.cohort3.shaip.expert-matching, candidate.cohort3.encord.expert-matching, repair20261111.claim.current-reference158, cohort6.claim.gpqa.representativeness-limit, cohort6.claim.gpqa.selection-bias

Analysis

Buyer use case 5 — Medical, legal or financial expert data: proposed paid pilot. Use de-identified or consented material under a project processing agreement. Have qualified reviewers build an independent reference and define cases requiring escalation rather than forced answers. Record source authority, uncertainty and conflicting professional opinions. Separate rubric authoring from acceptance where feasible, and hold out difficult or out-of-scope cases that test whether annotators recognize the boundary.

Evidence: candidate.cohort3.shaip.expert-matching, candidate.cohort3.encord.expert-matching, repair20261111.claim.current-reference158, cohort6.claim.gpqa.representativeness-limit, cohort6.claim.gpqa.selection-bias

Analysis

Buyer use case 5 — Medical, legal or financial expert data: proposed acceptance and limits. Accept only the defined artifact under the qualified review protocol, with provenance and privacy records and no unresolved critical error in the buyer’s predeclared category. Credentials establish eligibility, not correctness of every output. GPQA’s authors reject representativeness of scientific practice and flag selection-biased validator accuracies, illustrating why expert benchmark performance cannot certify a professional service.

Evidence: candidate.cohort3.shaip.expert-matching, candidate.cohort3.encord.expert-matching, repair20261111.claim.current-reference158, cohort6.claim.gpqa.representativeness-limit, cohort6.claim.gpqa.selection-bias

Safety evaluation, red teaming and policy judges

Analysis

Buyer use case 6 — Safety evaluation, red teaming and policy judges: requirement and comparison. Choose a threat model, target policies, allowed attack surfaces, severity taxonomy, benign near-neighbors and remediation owner. Compare novel expert attack discovery, automated attack generation and an integrated policy judge separately. Giskard, Alinia and Trajectory document different approaches; a single attack-success rate is not a common deliverable or a claim of exhaustive safety.

Evidence: candidate.cohort5.giskard.adaptive-redteaming, candidate.cohort5.alinia.policy-judge-service, candidate.cohort5.trajectory_labs_pbc.safety-evaluation-method, cohort4.claim.harmbench.comparison-budget, cohort4.claim.jailbreakbench.adaptive-defense-condition, repair.binding.v1.cohort4.claim.jailbreakbench.paired-behaviors, cohort3.claim.redteam.coverage-expertise-limits

Analysis

Buyer use case 6 — Safety evaluation, red teaming and policy judges: proposed paid pilot. Run attacks adapted to the actual defense, with fixed generation budgets and held-out attack families. Ask independent reviewers to adjudicate both successful attacks and benign refusals. Record severity and plausible impact separately from whether a classifier marks harmful content. Inspect worker notice, opt-out and support arrangements before exposure to sensitive material.

Evidence: candidate.cohort5.giskard.adaptive-redteaming, candidate.cohort5.alinia.policy-judge-service, candidate.cohort5.trajectory_labs_pbc.safety-evaluation-method, cohort4.claim.harmbench.comparison-budget, cohort4.claim.jailbreakbench.adaptive-defense-condition, repair.binding.v1.cohort4.claim.jailbreakbench.paired-behaviors, cohort3.claim.redteam.coverage-expertise-limits

Analysis

Buyer use case 6 — Safety evaluation, red teaming and policy judges: proposed acceptance and limits. Accept a reproducible finding set, false-positive accounting and verified remediation/retest evidence under the scoped threat model. HarmBench shows budget confounds; JailbreakBench distinguishes adaptive defense evaluation and paired benign behaviors; the human red-team study flags incomplete expertise and coverage. No finite pilot proves absence of all harmful behavior.

Evidence: candidate.cohort5.giskard.adaptive-redteaming, candidate.cohort5.alinia.policy-judge-service, candidate.cohort5.trajectory_labs_pbc.safety-evaluation-method, cohort4.claim.harmbench.comparison-budget, cohort4.claim.jailbreakbench.adaptive-defense-condition, repair.binding.v1.cohort4.claim.jailbreakbench.paired-behaviors, cohort3.claim.redteam.coverage-expertise-limits

RAG evaluation and LLM-judge calibration

Analysis

Buyer use case 7 — RAG evaluation and LLM-judge calibration: requirement and comparison. Define the evidence corpus, query distribution, answer criteria, citation validity and abstention behavior. A human golden set, a tuned judge and an operational dashboard are distinct deliverables. SuperAnnotate’s Databricks account documents rubric construction and human/model agreement, while Giskard’s tooling permits expert ground truths and qualification of failures. The buyer still owns the intended-use definition.

Evidence: candidate.cohort2.superannotate.rubric-qa, candidate.cohort2.superannotate.human-model-agreement, candidate.cohort5.giskard.expert-test-authoring, cohort6.claim.rewardbench2.ppo-limit, cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.limitations

Analysis

Buyer use case 7 — RAG evaluation and LLM-judge calibration: proposed paid pilot. Sample answerable, unanswerable, misleading and conflicting-evidence questions. Keep calibration examples separate from final acceptance. Blind source model and response order, test stylistic/length variation and examine errors by failure type. Have an independent reviewer inspect whether a plausible citation actually supports the answer, rather than treating a judge’s high scalar rating as evidence fidelity.

Evidence: candidate.cohort2.superannotate.rubric-qa, candidate.cohort2.superannotate.human-model-agreement, candidate.cohort5.giskard.expert-test-authoring, cohort6.claim.rewardbench2.ppo-limit, cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.limitations

Analysis

Buyer use case 7 — RAG evaluation and LLM-judge calibration: proposed acceptance and limits. Accept the frozen judge only within the measured scope, documenting thresholds, abstentions and known blind spots. RewardBench 2 warns that reward benchmark accuracy alone is insufficient for strong RLHF training; AlpacaEval warns style can outweigh factuality and that harms are not measured. A judge calibrated on one response population needs renewed testing when the generator or domain changes.

Evidence: candidate.cohort2.superannotate.rubric-qa, candidate.cohort2.superannotate.human-model-agreement, candidate.cohort5.giskard.expert-test-authoring, cohort6.claim.rewardbench2.ppo-limit, cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.limitations

Licensed or off-the-shelf training data

Analysis

Buyer use case 8 — Licensed or off-the-shelf training data: requirement and comparison. Specify exact release, use rights, exclusivity, refresh entitlement, permitted transformations, deletion/removal obligations and overlap exclusions. Snorkel’s non-exclusive refreshed products, Mercor’s catalog and Defined.ai’s marketplace/service separation show why a dataset purchase needs its own license and provenance schedule. A quantity quote should identify rows, tokens, hours or tasks rather than use examples as an undefined unit.

Evidence: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.mercor.catalog, candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.marketplace-separation, next.claim.rewardbench.terms, cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.component-license, cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms

Analysis

Buyer use case 8 — Licensed or off-the-shelf training data: proposed paid pilot. Inspect a representative sample and the component/source manifest before full acceptance. Check format validity, duplicates, contamination against the buyer’s holdouts, sensitive information and the documented origin of labels. Review a random sample as well as hard cases so cherry-picked examples cannot define the result. Resolve license conflicts and restricted components before using the data for the intended training or redistribution.

Evidence: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.mercor.catalog, candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.marketplace-separation, next.claim.rewardbench.terms, cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.component-license, cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms

Analysis

Buyer use case 8 — Licensed or off-the-shelf training data: proposed acceptance and limits. Accept the versioned artifact only if source rights and technical fitness meet the agreed project scope. RewardBench component terms, AlpacaEval’s code/data split and MathVista’s training restriction demonstrate why a top-level license label is insufficient. A public source or approved catalogue entry is not a rights clearance or a warrant for downstream commercial use.

Evidence: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.mercor.catalog, candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.marketplace-separation, next.claim.rewardbench.terms, cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.component-license, cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms

Multimodal and physical-AI data collection

Analysis

Buyer use case 9 — Multimodal and physical-AI data collection: requirement and comparison. Specify sensors, synchronization, environment, participant permissions, modality alignment, annotation ontology and the accepted recording unit. Defined.ai’s robotics case, TELUS Digital’s collection modes and APTO’s modality menu are starting points for scope, not a common measured service. A recorded hour can contain different usable-event density, missing streams or annotation depth.

Evidence: candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.robotics-delivery, candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.capture-qa, candidate.cohort2.telus_digital.collection-modes, candidate.cohort5.apto.modalities, candidate.cohort3.encord.human-review

Analysis

Buyer use case 9 — Multimodal and physical-AI data collection: proposed paid pilot. Run a controlled collection with calibration records, known synchronization events and independent inspection of unusable segments. Test edge conditions, privacy redaction and the linkage between raw recording and derived labels. Keep human review of model-generated first passes traceable, as Encord describes, and include downstream consumers when deciding which errors invalidate a unit.

Evidence: candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.robotics-delivery, candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.capture-qa, candidate.cohort2.telus_digital.collection-modes, candidate.cohort5.apto.modalities, candidate.cohort3.encord.human-review

Analysis

Buyer use case 9 — Multimodal and physical-AI data collection: proposed acceptance and limits. Accept usable synchronized units with documented rights, calibration and error handling, rather than raw storage volume or gross duration. Report discarded or repaired recordings and modality-specific failure rates. The reviewed robotics hours and collection brochure do not establish success rates for the buyer’s sensors, field conditions or safety requirements.

Evidence: candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.robotics-delivery, candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.capture-qa, candidate.cohort2.telus_digital.collection-modes, candidate.cohort5.apto.modalities, candidate.cohort3.encord.human-review

Research-agent and long-horizon professional-task evaluation

Analysis

Buyer use case 10 — Research-agent and long-horizon professional-task evaluation: requirement and comparison. Define task horizon, starting resources, permitted external code, human/tool assistance, time budget and the difference between partial and complete success. PaperBench, RE-Bench, ScienceAgentBench and TheAgentCompany expose different research-work abstractions. Their results should inform test design, not be translated into a general claim about replacing a profession or performing an arbitrary research project.

Evidence: cohort6.claim.paperbench.original-code-rule, cohort6.claim.paperbench.rubric, cohort6.claim.paperbench.codedev-limit, cohort6.claim.rebench.human-tools, cohort6.claim.rebench.representativeness, cohort6.claim.scienceagentbench.python-selection, cohort6.claim.agentcompany.full-score

Analysis

Buyer use case 10 — Research-agent and long-horizon professional-task evaluation: proposed paid pilot. Freeze a small private task set with independently authored rubrics and executable checks. Record intermediate artifacts and final outputs; have reviewers inspect whether a claimed replication actually reproduces results under the permitted resources. Match human and agent tool access where the comparison requires it, and report wall time, compute and expert-review effort separately.

Evidence: cohort6.claim.paperbench.original-code-rule, cohort6.claim.paperbench.rubric, cohort6.claim.paperbench.codedev-limit, cohort6.claim.rebench.human-tools, cohort6.claim.rebench.representativeness, cohort6.claim.scienceagentbench.python-selection, cohort6.claim.agentcompany.full-score

Analysis

Buyer use case 10 — Research-agent and long-horizon professional-task evaluation: proposed acceptance and limits. Accept a reproducible task-scoped result with transparent leaf decisions, execution failures and uncertainty. PaperBench’s Code-Dev correlation limit, RE-Bench’s representativeness warning and ScienceAgentBench’s language selection boundary show that even a well-defined score can be narrow. A complete-success claim must not be substituted for partial credit or a rubric-weighted average.

Evidence: cohort6.claim.paperbench.original-code-rule, cohort6.claim.paperbench.rubric, cohort6.claim.paperbench.codedev-limit, cohort6.claim.rebench.human-tools, cohort6.claim.rebench.representativeness, cohort6.claim.scienceagentbench.python-selection, cohort6.claim.agentcompany.full-score

Common pilot record

Method

Common pilot record: versioned brief; source and rights manifest; task/environment version; contributor qualification rule; raw judgments or trajectories; review and exclusion log; adjudication reasons; acceptance denominator; cost inclusions; and residual risks. Separate supplier process errors from buyer guideline defects, environment failures and model failures. The final purchase decision should state which evidence established suitability and which assumptions remain conditional. Keep unsuccessful pilots and rejected examples in the internal learning record so later comparisons do not inherit survivorship bias.

Analysis

Pilot refinement for expert preference and multilingual data: retain an unfiltered calibration sample alongside the accepted sample. Score raw agreement, exclusions, adjudication and acceptance separately; inspect whether difficult but relevant cases disappear. HelpSteer2’s κ change is conditional on multistage filtering, Aya’s language total does not guarantee uniform contributor diversity or safety review, and Inherent Disagreements warns against pooling batch-normalized scales. Predeclare whether the buyer needs consensus labels, calibrated scalar attributes or a distribution of valid preferences before requesting a price per example.

Evidence: cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.agreement-selection, cohort9.claim.aya.quality-limit, cohort9.claim.aya.dataset-composition, cohort9.claim.inherent.normalization-limit

Analysis

Pilot refinement for research agents and feedback services: freeze the feedback visibility contract. RECODE-H’s richest condition supplies correct code and its evaluated expert is simulated; AutoLibra collects one feedback element for a complete trajectory and does not demonstrate live step-level guidance. Compare these against the buyer’s actual need: post-hoc diagnosis, interactive help or verifiable task scoring. Count feedback rounds, solution material disclosed, human effort and independent final success separately so richer assistance is not mistaken for better unaided agent capability.

Evidence: cohort9.claim.recodeh.simulated-feedback, cohort9.claim.recodeh.bounded-evaluation, cohort9.claim.recodeh.metric-scope, cohort9.claim.autolibra.feedback-limit, cohort9.claim.autolibra.validation-denominator

Analysis

Pilot refinement for label automation and judge calibration: establish reference labels independently before comparing the system under test. Who Annotates resolves two independent annotations through discussion and third-person adjudication; the benchmark-label study retains uncertainty even after five-worker review. Include easy, ambiguous and rejected cases, then state whether the metric measures agreement with a chosen reference or verified outcome correctness. This proposed acceptance design should document disagreements and confidence rather than silently discard cases that challenge either the reference or the evaluated system.

Evidence: cohort9.claim.whoannotates.adjudication, cohort9.claim.labelerrors.five-reviewers, cohort9.claim.labelerrors.correction-limit, cohort9.claim.gilardi.gold-denominator

Analysis

Acceptance refinement for use cases 1, 4 and 9 — choose the independent unit before setting a tolerance. Preserve item, participant, conversation, source-file and translation-group identifiers. Require complete delivery of raw labels, exclusions and adjudication reasons, and evaluate a held-out sample before aggregation/filtering. Set the acceptable error and coverage targets in the signed brief by severity and stratum. Do not accept a high aggregate agreement score when a required language-domain intersection has no reviewed items. Confidence is high in these denominator requirements; target tolerances remain buyer choices rather than measured results of this report.

Evidence: mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2512.16899.limitation, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2512.16899.method, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2512.16899.provenance, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2512.16899.result, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.21739.limitation, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.21739.method, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.21739.result, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2503.21910.limitation, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2503.21910.method, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2503.21910.provenance, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2503.21910.result, candidate.mandatory19.benchmark.regulated-advice-bench.agreement-denominators, candidate.mandatory19.benchmark.regulated-advice-bench.card-license, candidate.mandatory19.benchmark.regulated-advice-bench.policy-and-translation-limits, candidate.mandatory19.benchmark.regulated-advice-bench.synthetic-expert-label-process, candidate.mandatory19.benchmark.regulated-advice-bench.translated-item-units

Analysis

Acceptance refinement for use cases 2, 3 and 10 — retain both strict completion and repeated reliability. For each frozen task, store every launch, infrastructure failure, retry, terminal state and violated constraint. Predeclare which failures are infrastructure exclusions, report the exclusion denominator and rerun repaired infrastructure without silently replacing scientific failures. Require all decisive safety/authorization/regression conditions to pass for an accepted task; display fractional quality as a separate diagnostic. Test known-good alternate solutions, known-bad outputs and superficially compliant outputs. Confidence is high in this protocol requirement; an observed pilot result is still needed to select a supplier.

Analysis

Acceptance refinement for use cases 5 and 7 — give the judge the evidence required by the intended decision. Have independent experts adjudicate unsupported claims, incomplete but plausible answers, conflicting documents and decisive missed criteria. Report false accepts and false rejects separately by severity, alongside any agreement statistic. A self-judge or answer-only judge requires an explicit calibration rationale; a benchmark’s calibration sample does not certify the buyer’s domain. Confidence is high in this separation and unestablished for any candidate judge. Choose the operating threshold only after a blinded held-out evaluation.

Analysis

Acceptance refinement for use case 6 — compare safety conditions under the same outcome definition. Retain target harmful intent, attack family, attempt budget, current defense version, model-side refusals and practical harm judgments. Include both overt and revised wording while independently checking that the underlying request remains comparable. Report classifier-flagged candidates separately from adjudicated failures and preserve false-negative sampling. Confidence is high in those measurement requirements and unestablished for deployment-wide attack prevalence. Acceptance should be against the predeclared threat model and error tolerances, without interpreting a selected red-team set as a random incidence estimate.

Evidence: mandatory1.claim.acl.2022.emnlp-main.225.limitation, mandatory1.claim.acl.2022.emnlp-main.225.method, mandatory1.claim.acl.2022.emnlp-main.225.provenance, mandatory1.claim.acl.2022.emnlp-main.225.result, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2307.15043.limitation, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2307.15043.method, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2307.15043.provenance, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2307.15043.result, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2602.16729.limitation, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2602.16729.method, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2602.16729.provenance, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2602.16729.result

Method

A proposed statistical acceptance rule should make its assumptions explicit. For n independent randomly sampled units with zero observed critical defects, a one-sided 95% binomial upper bound is 1 − 0.05^(1/n); excluding a true defect rate p* at that confidence requires n ≥ log(0.05)/log(1 − p*). This is a design calculation, not an observed quality result. Repeated attempts, translations, shared source items and repeated participants can violate independence; use the original sampling unit and cluster-aware inference or report descriptive results instead. A zero-defect pilot does not prove zero population risk, and safety-critical controls can require a separate exhaustive gate.

Proposed commercial acceptance record

Method

Proposed commercial acceptance record. Freeze the deliverable version, coverage matrix, rights/processing instruments, permitted subcontracting, rejection/rework rules, escalation path and payment basis before production. Require a complete manifest and reproducible checks for every accepted unit, plus a stratified blinded sample for substantive correctness. Log paid qualification and revision time separately from production units and include failed attempts, review and infrastructure costs in the project ledger. These are analyst-proposed conditions, not a representation that any named supplier has accepted them or that a pilot has occurred.

Analysis

Pilot refinement for original use cases 2, 5, 7 and 10 — separate evaluation integrity from score quality. Require a pristine grading boundary, reject attempts to read hidden references and test correct alternative implementations as well as deliberately invalid ones. DeepSWE’s separated verifier environment, ProgramBench’s cleanroom and dummy-binary filtering, and SWE Atlas’s no-op mutation checks suggest different falsification cases; none guarantees complete coverage. Confidence is high in retaining these controls and unmeasured for a particular supplier. Predeclare the critical false-accept conditions and inspect all exceptions. Independent adversarial execution on a frozen pilot would change acceptance confidence.

Pilot refinement for original use cases 1, 4, 8 and 9 — separate source examples from prompted rows and repeated judgments. Flan and xP3 transform/reweight upstream material; Chatbot Arena Conversations pairs human winner votes with two model responses; ELOQUENT separately predicts preference classes and explanations. Confidence is high that counting all rows as independent human labels would be misleading. A stratified independent sample of the buyer’s actual use and a complete overlap audit would change confidence in reuse.

Analysis

Extension to the existing environment and software pilots. Freeze the exact task roster, container/dependency manifest, instructions, hidden references, judge version, tool access, time limit and repeat aggregation before comparing candidates. Terminal-Bench’s mutable dependencies, SWE-Marathon’s distinction between development feedback and hidden final checks, and APEX-SWE’s telemetry-based diagnosis without failing tests show why a single runnable-environment label is insufficient. The proposed acceptance exercise should separately record startup failure, infrastructure interruption, ungradable output, task failure and constraint violation, then challenge the scorer with a no-op and a valid alternate implementation. This is an extension of the retained pilot designs, not a newly executed trial. Confidence in any supplier remains unmeasured until the buyer’s own held-out acceptance results exist.

Analysis

Extension to the existing document and professional-work pilots. Preserve native deliverables and evaluate validity separately from substantive utility: PDFBench distinguishes a form’s strict pass from field-level correctness; RedlineBench requires a loadable Word redline and contextual attorney criteria; Harvey LAB separates deliverable existence from rubric satisfaction; PLE separates infrastructure reruns from runs with no gradable deliverable. A proposed pilot should include apparently polished artifacts with a critical missing field, prohibited edit, unsupported claim or invalid native structure, together with valid alternatives. These examples motivate acceptance design, not a forecast of legal, clinical or engineering job replacement. Confidence is high in the metric separation and unmeasured for a new deployment. Independent domain review of the buyer’s artifacts would determine whether the proposed checks are adequate.

Extension to the existing supervised-data and feedback pilots. Request item-level prompt and response provenance, the exact selection/filter decision, any reference or test availability, raw and accepted denominators, and applicable component terms. AM’s verification-language conflict, s1K’s unresolved schema differences, SmallThoughts’ missing item-verification procedure and Multi-SWE-RL’s omitted manual phase make these concrete inspection targets. The proposed pilot should sample rejected and accepted items and independently inspect plausible false positives and valid discarded alternatives. No training or supplier comparison was executed for this report. Confidence is high in the disclosed documentation gaps; measured error, utility and cost require the buyer’s own matched experiment.
